Description: Students gain an overview of research and theory in educational psychology and explore their applications in teaching and learning.
Prerequisites: PSY 1000, EDU 2110, EDU 2500, or SOC 2430
Course Types: Advanced Studies, Poverty and Social Justice Studies Elective, Teaching and Learning Elective

Title: Nonexperimental Research Methods and Statistics
Description: Students learn how to design, review and analyze nonexperimental psychological research. The course focuses on developing research questions, answering them using nonexperimental research designs and complementary data analysis techniques, and the basics of writing research reports.
Prerequisites: PSY 2970

Title: Evolutionary Psychology
Description: Evolutionary Psychology uses the biological theory of evolution as a basis for understanding human behavior. Through exposure to primary and secondary source material, this course will cover basic principles of evolutionary theory, psychological topics that have been informed by evolutionary theory (e.g., prosocial behavior, aggression, cognition, and interpersonal interaction), and current debates on how and whether evolutionary theory ought to be applied to our understanding of human psychology.
Prerequisites: PSY 1000

Title: Industrial and Organizational Psychology
Description: Psychological applications in the workplace are the focus of this course. Topics include personnel selection, leadership and motivation, job satisfaction and work performance.
Prerequisites: PSY 1000

Title: Teaching and Learning Apprenticeship
Description: Teaching and Learning Apprentices work with a faculty mentor on a particular course. This experience is intended for exceptional students who wish to deepen their knowledge of the discipline, gain a better understanding of the professional academic life, engage in a meaningful mentoring relationship with a faculty mentor around issues related to teaching, enhance their interpersonal and communication skills, and develop their leadership skills. The experience may be of particular value to students who wish to pursue a career in higher education or teaching in general. Faculty members invite students to consider a 4990 experience.
Prerequisites: Requires satisfactory completion of all requirements listed on the registration form

Title: Empirical Research Seminar
Description: In this capstone course, students read primary sources to identify and critically evaluate the major theoretical and empirical foundations of one topic area in the field of psychology. With faculty supervision, students devise, conduct and report an original empirical investigation of a question related to the selected area of concern. Students present their work orally as well as in a well developed, integrated APA-style manuscript.
Prerequisites: PSY 2970, PSY 3970, and Psychology major with senior standing.

Title: Internship in Psychology
Description: Upper-level psychology majors apply psychological theories and techniques to actual experiences in the field.
Prerequisites: Psychology major and faculty approval
Course Types: Advanced Studies; Experiential Learning Requirement; Internship

Title: Senior Seminar
Description: In this capstone course, students will read primary sources and identify and critically evaluate theoretical issues and empirical findings of one topic area in the field of psychology. With faculty supervision, students will develop and present (in both written and oral formats) a thesis-level integrative literature review manuscript.
Prerequisites: PSY 2970; PSY 3970; and Psychology major with senior standing,

Title: Research
Description: In collaboration with a psychology faculty member, students undertake an empirical or theoretical study of a topic in psychology. Research projects may include a review of the relevant research literature, data collection and analysis, and a presentation or report when the study is completed.
Prerequisites: PSY 1000, sophomore, junior, or senior status, and permission of instructor

Title: Senior Seminar in Public Policy
Description: The Senior Seminar in Public Policy is designed as a capstone experience in which students will apply the knowledge and skills acquired through their academic course work and internships either to a research project or to a community based problem.
Prerequisites: POL 2200, PUB 1000 and senior standing
